x: The "Centenary" Cup, the equivalent award for women went to Helen Alsop née Maskrey who led the Belgrave team to the bronze medals in the AAA Marathon, held in conjunction with the 2000 London Marathon.

Helen Alsop, team captain and running in her first National road relay was nervous, but confident that she wouldn't lose many places over the course.

Helen Alsop was also well pleased with her sub 11 minutes time in the 3,000 metres which was won emphatically by Harrow's Andrea Whitcombe, past national cross country champion and currently a successful triathlete.
An unfit Tania Sturton had a torrid time trying to hold things together on lap two but with Syreeta Stracey and Helen Alsop both pulling back places it was bronze medals for the Belles again.

With the Belles maintaining a steady position towards the top of the field Helen Alsop took over on the third leg intending to improve on last year's time and bring the team home in a position where Getenesh could challenge the front runners.
